title: Ben Stokes Retires. The Man Who Defined a Generation of England Cricket — and Haunted India Along the Way.
excerpt: The 35-year-old all-rounder announced his retirement mid-match at Trent Bridge, then took a wicket with his first ball and opened the batting with two sixes. For Indian cricket fans, he was the rival you couldn't look away from.
body:
Ben Stokes chose the most Ben Stokes way to announce his retirement from international cricket. Not a press conference. Not a social media post the night before. He told his teammates in the Trent Bridge dressing room on Sunday morning, mid-Test, with England facing a near-impossible chase against New Zealand. Then he walked out, took a wicket with his very first ball, and opened the batting — hitting two sixes in the first five overs.

Of course he did.

The England and Wales Cricket Board confirmed the 35-year-old would step away from international cricket after the ongoing third Test against New Zealand. Stokes is playing in his 122nd Test, alongside 114 ODIs and 43 T20 Internationals. The crowd at Trent Bridge gave him a standing ovation the moment the news broke. New Zealand's players formed a guard of honour when he led England back onto the field.

## The Bazball Captain

Stokes took over the England Test captaincy in 2022 and, alongside coach Brendon McCullum, launched what became known as 'Bazball' — a philosophy of relentless aggression that divided opinion worldwide but transformed England's Test cricket. In his four and a half years at the helm, Stokes pushed his team to play fearlessly, even when conventional wisdom screamed otherwise. It won matches, lost matches, and created some of the most entertaining cricket this decade.

"It's the best thing that I've ever been asked to do, captaining this team, captaining this country," Stokes told Sky Sports. "But there's another side to it that people don't see. The responsibility has burned me out."

He revealed that a head injury during a training session had brought back difficult memories, and the emotional toll of captaincy had finally caught up with him. "I put so much time and effort into putting things right and I just burned myself out," he said.

## India's Favourite Rival

For Indian cricket fans — and for the millions of NRIs who follow every England-India contest — Stokes was the opponent you grudgingly respected and quietly feared.

His career is woven into some of India's most painful and celebrated cricket memories. In 2019, India's devastating semifinal exit from the World Cup paved the way for an England-New Zealand final where Stokes' unbeaten 84 delivered England their maiden 50-over title. Indian fans watched that innings with a cocktail of admiration and what-might-have-been.

In 2016, Stokes scored a Test century at Rajkot that marked him as a genuine all-round threat in Indian conditions. Last summer, at Old Trafford, he hammered 141 against India in a drawn fourth Test — a knock that had Indian bowlers shaking their heads.

And then there was the T20 World Cup 2026 semifinal at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. Stokes' England fell agonisingly short against India, losing 246/7 to 253/7. It was the kind of theatre that defined his career. He was always in the biggest moments — even when they didn't go his way.

Virat Kohli captured the relationship best when Stokes retired from ODI cricket: "You're the most competitive bloke I've ever played against. Respect."

## One Last Afternoon

True to form, Stokes' final afternoon was extraordinary. After taking the wicket of Zak Foulkes with his first ball post-announcement — sprinting away in wild celebration as teammates mobbed him — he then walked out to open the batting in England's chase of 373. It was only the third time in his career he had opened in Tests.

He scored 30 off 20 balls, all sixes and intent, before holing out. England finished Day 3 at 103/4. Trent Bridge has announced that entry will be free for his final day of international cricket on Monday.

Stokes will continue playing for Durham in county cricket, but international cricket has lost one of its genuine icons. For NRIs in England who watched him at Lord's, The Oval, and Headingley — and for Indian fans everywhere who measured their own heroes against him — this feels like the end of an era.

India tour England for three ODIs starting July 14 at Edgbaston. For the first time in over a decade, Stokes won't be on the other side. English cricket will feel different. Indian fans might even miss him.

*Sources: Reuters, ECB, The Sun, ESPN Cricinfo, Wikipedia*
